properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"The graph is the index of its own snapshots","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Git already stores versions, tags, branches and releases well, and reflow2 must not duplicate that. What reflow2 must own is the MAP: the graph tracks its own snapshots — which epoch_n or increment_n a thing belongs to, and where that snapshot lives (the git ref) — so a user asks the graph and never has to remember which branch holds which epoch. Anthony, 2026-07-28: 'what does this mean for reflow2 when most of what I discussed is what git already does? I think the answer is that the graph should track the snapshots (it is one graph in time) and therefore which epoch_n or increment_n something is. A user shouldn't have to remember which git branch a particular epoch or increment is in.' The in-repo precedent already exists for the backward direction: rel:v0180 lives in the graph, tag v0.18.0 lives in git, and the graph node names the version — nobody greps tags to learn what shipped. This requirement extends that same division of labor forward.","status":"proposed"}
